body:
Added a test case for this. 

I think the issue itself is too hard for myself to fix on my own though.

Looking through the changes to from 0.2.32 to 0.2.33, I found this PR https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/3160, which might have something to do with this. But it's just a guess.

Wow.  That's definitely weird.

Ran your tests, see it happening.  You can sort of fix it by removing the join from `StageType` -> `Stage`

I reverted that PR and ran your tests without any changes & it does resolve the issue.

Thanks @hehall for creating this issue.
I have noticed the same problem after upgrading from 0.2.24 to >= 0.2.33 <= 0.2.37.
0.2.32 do not have this issue.

I agree with Aereksio that the PR has definitely broken other things.
I am not entirely sure this is the exact same issue, but it is probably related.
The assignment in this line 
https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/2adfe36627507ab5e01bc4bc7f6b4ec839a2352c/src/query-builder/transformer/RawSqlResultsToEntityTransformer.ts#L182 (introduced by https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/3160)
causes issues with `SelectQueryBuilder.getManyAndCount()`

Get many succeeds, however, once the result is mapped and the assignment above is run, an invalid count query is generated:
```sql
-- get many query
SELECT "LayoutEntity"."id"                  AS "LayoutEntity_id",
       "LayoutEntity_previews"."layoutId"   AS "LayoutEntity_previews_layoutId",
       "LayoutEntity_options"."id"          AS "LayoutEntity_options_id",
       "LayoutEntity_options"."name"        AS "LayoutEntity_options_name",
       "LayoutEntity_options"."type"        AS "LayoutEntity_options_type",
       "LayoutEntity_options_values"."uuid" AS "LayoutEntity_options_values_uuid",
       "previews"."cacheId"                 AS "previews_cacheId",
       "previews"."layoutId"                AS "previews_layoutId"
FROM "typeorm"."layout" "LayoutEntity"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_previews" "LayoutEntity_previews"
                   ON "LayoutEntity_previews"."layoutId" = "LayoutEntity"."id"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_option" "LayoutEntity_options"
                   ON "LayoutEntity_options"."layoutId" = "LayoutEntity"."id"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_option_value" "LayoutEntity_options_values"
                   ON "LayoutEntity_options_values"."layoutOptionId" = "LayoutEntity_options"."id"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_previews" "previews" ON "previews"."layoutId" = "LayoutEntity"."id"
ORDER BY "LayoutEntity"."id" ASC
LIMIT 50;

-- But when the count query tries to count, the original query is invalid
SELECT "LayoutEntity"."id"                  AS "LayoutEntity_id",
       "LayoutEntity_previews"."layoutId"   AS "LayoutEntity_previews_layoutId",
       "LayoutEntity_options"."id"          AS "LayoutEntity_options_id",
       "LayoutEntity_options"."name"        AS "LayoutEntity_options_name",
       "LayoutEntity_options"."type"        AS "LayoutEntity_options_type",
       "LayoutEntity_options_values"."uuid" AS "LayoutEntity_options_values_uuid",
       "previews"."cacheId"                 AS "previews_cacheId",
       "previews"."layoutId"                AS "previews_layoutId"
FROM "typeorm"."layout" "LayoutEntity"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_previews" "LayoutEntity_previews"
                   ON LayoutEntity_previews.layout.id = "LayoutEntity"."id" -- this line has an invalid join condition
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_option" "LayoutEntity_options"
                   ON "LayoutEntity_options"."layoutId" = "LayoutEntity"."id"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_option_value" "LayoutEntity_options_values"
                   ON "LayoutEntity_options_values"."layoutOptionId" = "LayoutEntity_options"."id"
         LEFT JOIN "typeorm"."layout_previews" "previews" ON "previews"."layoutId" = "LayoutEntity"."id"
ORDER BY "LayoutEntity"."id" ASC
LIMIT 50
```

I've had this happen on multiple occasions with different setups.
To get a basic idea of the structure of my entities, here is an overview of the structure in the form of a graphql query:
```gql
layouts(limit: 50) {
  previews {
    image720Url
  }
  options {
    values {
      previews {
        image720Url
      }
    }
  }
}
```
The code for the root entity (`LayoutEntity`) above can be found [here](https://github.com/ThemezerNX/API/blob/f0ea889e2d45e4cc8b6e9a6a9a9ce8a1b6657276/src/graphql/Layout/Layout.entity.ts)
Hope this could provide more info about the issue.

**Edit:** I tried without my custom naming strategy that overwrites `tableName()`, which fixes the issue.
However, when I hardcode the entity names like they would've been with the naming strategy, the issue is back.
It seems that if I name my entities differently, the issue does not occur.

**Temporary fix:**
I am also unable to bypass this by running the `getMany()` and `getCount()` manually, because the generated count query is still affected (when I use the same SelectQueryBuilder instance). Instead, simply cloning the `SelectQueryBuilder` _before_ calling `getMany()` and then calling `clonedBuilder.getCount()` works!
```
const clonedBuilder = queryBuilder.clone();
return {result: await queryBuilder.getMany(), count: await clonedBuilder.getCount()};
```

body:
@pleerock 
I acknowledge that the problem is serious. I had to commit 32 version to the project. I am very surprised at what the changes were made for and how crudely they were executed.
An explicit example of why this seemed to be done can be seen here: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/tree/master/test/functional/table-inheritance/single-table/relations/child-relation-type
At the moment, I observe the inability of the ORM to correctly define the class of the child entity. The problem is observed when fetching through the parent entity repository with connecting child joins.
Please exclude this change from the project.
The problem is not only in security, but also in data integrity, classes of child entities can be heterogeneous in data fields and have different relationships. As a result of incorrect mapping, the data of such entities will be partially lost.
